messages:
anya: Hey team — Acme POC still seeing slow first-token (TTFT) on Dedicated in their VPC. Customer says it was fine in hosted during trial. Any ideas?

tk: Noted. Are they on our Private appliance or Dedicated VPC peering?

mike: They opted for Dedicated + VPC egress via customer's NAT gateway. Seen that pattern before — NAT timeouts and TCP warmup can add 50-200ms on first request.

kate_seng: To add: we also observed cache invalidation spikes when model variant changes. If their orchestration flips models, KV cache miss rate jumps and TTFT suffers. Do we have logs showing model_id churn?

anya: Good call. Dan, can you paste the request logs for the failing time window (yesterday 14:12-14:40 UTC)?

infra-bot: deploy: dedicated-pool-42 scaled up +2 nodes at 2026-02-15T14:10:12Z.

dan_cust_sre: Pasting a condensed snippet below — sanitized.
dan_cust_sre: ```
2026-02-15T14:11:23Z | req_id=abc123 | model=redwood-3b-v1 | route=acme-prod | cache_hit=false | backend=dedicated-42 | ttft_ms=420
2026-02-15T14:11:55Z | req_id=abc124 | model=redwood-3b-v1 | cache_hit=true  | backend=dedicated-42 | ttft_ms=78
2026-02-15T14:12:10Z | req_id=abc130 | model=redwood-3b-v2 | cache_hit=false | backend=dedicated-42 | ttft_ms=510
```

laura_sec: Also saw some 429s around 14:12 from their side — might be client retry/backoff interacting with our burst limiter. Any rate-limit rules applied to the route?

mike: Route has token-bucket: burst=200 qps, sustained=120 qps. If client is sending many parallel cold sessions that can blow through and trigger immediate 429 + retries -> more cold starts.

tk: So potential combo: NAT+KV-cache-miss+burst-limits. Which one is dominant? We should prioritize deterministic items: cache and model churn.

anya: Agreed. Dan, can you run a quick grep for model switches in that timeframe? Something like \"rg \"model=redwood-3b\" /var/logs/requests* | awk\" — just need counts per model id.

dan_cust_sre: Ran it. Output: `redwood-3b-v1: 42 reqs, redwood-3b-v2: 9 reqs` in the 14:10-14:20 window. Not a ton of churn, but v2 requests clustered at the top of the window.

kate_seng: That clustering could explain a burst of cache misses while the rest hit warm cache. Also their client SDK spins up many short-lived connections (we saw many distinct connection IDs).

laura_sec: From security side, they put an outbound firewall that force-probes endpoints via a proxy healthcheck every minute — could be creating extra cold TCP resources.

mike: Suggested action list: 1) enable per-route warmup policy (keep-alive pings) for their Dedicated pool, 2) bump prefix caching TTL for that model during POC, 3) ask customer to use HTTP/2 persistent connections or our SDK, 4) temporarily relax burst protection for their route while we debug.

anya: I'll coordinate with Acme PM. Mike/tk — can you put together the exact commands/config to change warmup and prefix TTL? Keep changes reversible.

tk: Warmup: set `route[acme-prod].warmup.keepalive=30s` (control plane flag). Prefix TTL is on the model config: `model.redwood-3b*.prefix_ttl=60s` (was 10s in POC). Bumping to 60s should reduce KV misses.

mike: For burst relax: `route[acme-prod].rate_limit.override={burst:500}` — but only for a 30min window. I'll draft an ops playbook.

dan_cust_sre: Implemented warmup ping toggle on the pool (no restart). Observing immediate drop in median TTFT: 420ms -> 95ms within 3 minutes.

anya: Nice. Laura — security okay with temporary burst change?

laura_sec: Temporary increase approved for 30m while we monitor logs. Must revert at 14:55 UTC. Log retention rule: keep audit for this window.

anya: Customer update: they confirmed switching the SDK to our bundled client decreased connection churn. They still want written note on networking guidance (NAT config, keepalives).

kate_seng: I'll prepare a short doc snippet: \"Networking best practices for Dedicated/VPC: enable TCP keepalive, avoid short-lived connections, allow persistent HTTP/2, reserve NAT ports, prefer our SDK for connection pooling.\"

tk: One more thing — found evidence of a client-side exponential retry with no jitter in their integration. That amplified a small 429 spike into more load. Recommend adding jitter/backoff and honoring Retry-After.

anya: Great. Action items recap:
anya: - mike: draft ops playbook + perform burst override + revert schedule
anya: - tk: apply warmup + prefix TTL change (done)
anya: - kate: write networking guidance and send to Acme
anya: - laura: keep audit logs and confirm revert
anya: - dan: monitor and close loop with customer after 1h

mike: I'll post the playbook here in 10m.

dan_cust_sre: Monitoring link: https://console.redwood.example/obs/requests?route=acme-prod&from=2026-02-15T14:00Z

anya: Thanks all — setting a 30m check-in at 14:50 UTC. :thumbsup:

mike: playbook (short):
```
1) increase route burst to 500 (control plane)
2) enable warmup.keepalive=30s
3) increase prefix_ttl to 60s
4) monitor TTFT, cache_hit rate, and 429s
5) revert burst at scheduled time
```

anya: Thread resolved for now, will reopen if any regression.

infra-bot: alert: route acme-prod burst-override reverted at 2026-02-15T14:55:02Z.
